sourceCopy.examplesHeading: Four useful ways to get started

examples.heading: A number for a document
examples.text: 1234567 becomes one million two hundred thirty-four thousand five hundred sixty-seven.

examples.heading: Keep a small decimal clear
examples.text: -0.05 reads minus zero point zero five. Each fractional digit is spoken separately.

examples.heading: An identifier with leading zeroes
examples.text: 0012 reads zero zero one two in digit mode. Ordinary number words would instead describe twelve.

examples.heading: Round a dollar amount explicitly
examples.text: 1.995 rounds to 2.00 USD. The words are two dollars and zero cents.

method.heading: The rules behind the result
paragraphs: Ordinary mode uses English short-scale names. One billion means a thousand million, or 10^9. Groups of three digits are read from the highest nonzero group down to the units. This output uses US-style wording without an extra and inside ordinary whole numbers.

Tens between twenty-one and ninety-nine use a hyphen when they include a units digit. Hundreds are written as one hundred, two hundred and so on. Regional punctuation and style guides may prefer different connectors, even when the numeric value is the same.

Decimal digits are read one at a time after point. The input 1.05 becomes one point zero five. Trailing decimal zeroes remain audible: 1.50 reads one point five zero. Ordinary mode treats leading whole-number zeroes as formatting rather than a change of value.

Digit mode keeps those leading zeroes because each entered digit is part of the reading. That makes it more appropriate for an identifier or a code. A negative nonzero value receives minus. A numeric negative zero is not presented as a different amount.

US dollar mode rounds to the nearest cent, with half-cent ties away from zero. Rounding is performed using integer digits, rather than binary floating-point arithmetic. The rounded numeric amount is shown in the working. Verify the wording and rounding policy before using it on a financial document.

Named scales are provided through vigintillion, or 10^63. Larger whole numbers switch to an explicitly labelled digit-by-digit reading. The converter does not invent unfamiliar scale names or silently drop groups beyond a trillion. There is no fixed input-digit quota; practical output size depends on the device.

uses.heading: Use the result with the right context
paragraphs: Copy the result into a document, lesson or draft amount description. Select lowercase, title case or uppercase to suit the destination. Letter case changes presentation only; it does not alter the number or rounding.

For a code with meaningful leading zeroes, choose Read each digit rather than ordinary words. For a mathematical decimal, ordinary mode retains the fractional digits. The two modes answer different questions and make that choice visible.

This candidate produces English computational output. Interface translations and other languages need their own reviewed number-word rules. A translated button alone would not make an English algorithm correct for another language. Existing published language implementations are not replaced by this isolated prototype.

privacy.heading: Private calculations, clear limits
paragraphs: Your inputs and results stay in this browser. Calculation runs in a local worker, without a calculation API or uploaded data.
The page saves only your theme preference. A copied link contains the selected inputs and options, so share it deliberately.
Large calculations depend on device time and memory. Cancel stops the active job. An error clears old answers and disables their downloads.

faq.question: Which language does this candidate write?
faq.answer: English, using short-scale names and US-style whole-number wording. It does not claim translated number grammar for other languages.

faq.question: Can I enter a decimal?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a decimal point. Ordinary mode reads each fractional digit separately, including any trailing zeroes.

faq.question: Can it keep leading zeroes?
faq.answer: Choose Read each digit. The input 0012 becomes zero zero one two instead of the ordinary number twelve.

faq.question: What does one billion mean here?
faq.answer: It means 1,000,000,000 in the English short scale. Other historical or regional scale conventions may differ.

faq.question: How are dollar amounts rounded?
faq.answer: They are rounded to the nearest cent using integer arithmetic. Half-cent ties round away from zero.

faq.question: Why did a huge value switch to digit reading?
faq.answer: Named scales stop at vigintillion. Larger values use an explicit digit-by-digit reading to preserve every digit without inventing a scale name.

faq.question: Does this lose precision above a trillion?
faq.answer: No. Whole-number digits remain strings or BigInt values. The old twelve-digit restriction is not applied.

faq.question: Can I paste thousands separators?
faq.answer: No. Enter plain digits with an optional decimal point. This avoids guessing whether a comma means a decimal or a group separator.

faq.question: Can I change capitalization?
faq.answer: Yes. Lowercase, title case and uppercase are available. Hyphens and the numeric meaning remain the same.

faq.question: Is this a certified check-writing service?
faq.answer: No. It creates draft wording. Check the amount, currency, rounding and your bank’s requirements before using a financial document.
